text:
maria: quick follow-up on the rfc thread — proposing a smaller, more tactical approach to the hosted/dedicated/private handshake. want to avoid another giant capability manifest PR.
kevin: +1. what are you thinking?
nina: we should be careful — previous manifests got too big and stalled rollouts.
omar: agree. maybe a feature-flag first strategy? ship a minimal contract surface behind flags, iterate.
maria: exactly. proposal outline: 1) define a tiny "probe contract" that all runtimes implement (probe, health, capability-tag). 2) add a lightweight per-request header: X-RW-Deploy-Flags with comma list. 3) introduce ephemeral handoff tokens for secret-rebind operations. all opt-in.
kevin: ephemeral handoff tokens? can you sketch flow?
maria: flow: control plane issues a short-lived token when a tenant needs a secret rebind between hosted and private. runtime validates token with control plane, exchanges it for a scoped credential, then invalidates token. no long-lived cross-env secrets.
nina: that helps audits and reduces KMS surface. but how do we guarantee tokens can't be replayed across regions?
omar: token includes region, intended runtime id, and nonce signed by control plane. runtime checks nonce + last-seen to avoid replay. small DB on runtime side to track recent nonces — TTL short (30s).
kevin: sounds fine. concerns: added latency for on-path validation with control plane. if control plane is unavailable, we need fallback.
maria: plan B: token type A = online-validate; token type B = offline-signed-with-caveat (short TTL + aud claim). runtime can accept offline tokens if offline mode enabled in flag. fallback allowed only for non-privileged tenants.
deploybot: deploy scheduled: probe-contract v0.1 feature-flag rollout to canary cluster at 03:00 UTC :rocket:
nina: nice. another open question: KV-cache affinity and warmup. if we route to dedicated GPUs but cache is cold, latency spikes. can we surface a per-tenant "cache-warm" flag so control plane does a proactive kvcache-fill before switch?
omar: yes, control plane can request a prewarm call with probe header: X-RW-Deploy-Flags=prewarm. runtime will prioritize a warmup task with lower priority eviction.
kevin: also need to think about model-variant fallbacks across modes. hosted might have latest quantized variant, private might run older fp16. how do we preserve API parity?
maria: we don't. instead we publish a compatibility matrix per model: declared response-level equivalence tags. client can opt into "strict-compat" header to force a model variant that meets quality threshold, or accept approximate. documentability + telemetry are key.
nina: telemetry: need consistent trace headers across modes, and include flag and token metadata (no secrets) so quality monitoring and SLO accounting work.
omar: agree. implement trace propagation: X-RW-Trace + X-RW-Deploy-Flags in every hop. control plane logs token_id only. runtime emits token_id as hashed id in traces to make it linkable but not leak secrets.
nina: ops-wise, add a "stall window" concept on handoff: if runtime can't validate token online, wait up to 60s for control plane before failing hard. gives us brief reconciliation window during rolling upgrades.
kevin: lol (typo)
maria: acceptance criteria for probe-contract v0.1: - implement probe endpoint (GET /probe) that returns JSON blob with capability tags - runtime honors X-RW-Deploy-Flags: prewarm, offline-accept, strict-compat - control plane can mint ephemeral handoff tokens and audit them.
omar: risk list: nonce-store adds small state to runtime; offline tokens must be carefully scoped or they become an attack surface; prewarm could be abused to DoS if not rate-limited.
nina: mitigation: rate limits on prewarm per-tenant, token TTL < 2m, and admission policy that only allows prewarm for tenants with warmup quota.
maria: next steps: i'll draft a short spec (1-2 pages) with sequence diagrams and a small example curl flow. kevin/nina/omar — can you review by EOD Thursday?
kevin: yup
omar: will do
nina: yes, I'll review.
maria: thanks all. tagging this thread as follow-up for the rfc. if anyone thinks this is too fiddly we can trim offline tokens and start with only online-validated handoff. :+1:
deploybot: probe-contract v0.1 flag created: arch/probe-contract-flag (canary) — watchers: @maria @kevin @nina @omar
